title: Attention telemetry: histogram-driven profiling sprint notes
body:
Purpose and context:
This doc captures a short sprint (2 weeks) of work aimed at turning raw request telemetry into actionable microbenchmarks for attention kernels. Focus: build reproducible histograms, split signal by kernel selection, and design chasing experiments that isolate FlashAttention vs paged-attn vs fused ops regression surface.

Why histograms?
- Single-aggregate averages hide tails and multi-modal behavior.
- We observe multi-modal per-token latencies due to kernel switching and kv-cache hot/cold patterns; histograms let us decompose mixtures.

Telemetry sources and signals we used:
- per-request trace (trace_id, route, model, kernel_tag, seq_len, tokens_generated, warmup_flag)
- per-token timing (emit timestamp, kernel_start, kernel_end) sampled at 1% to reduce ingestion cost
- GPU-side counters (sm_eff, sm_occupancy, l2_bw_util, tensorcore_util) pulled from metrics exporter
- scheduler/batcher metrics (batch_size, queued_ms, coalesced_count)

Quick definitions (team glossary):
- kernel_tag: string label assigned by runtime before dispatch (flashpaged, flash, paged, fused-opset-V2)
- warmup_flag: true if request triggered kernel priming path or cache-priming sequence length
- kv-hot: request whose prefix hits highly in prefix-cache (based on overlap > 0.6)

What we collected (method):
1) Retrospective: pulled last 7 days of route-level traces for model 'redwood-3b-v1' across two regions.
2) Built histogram buckets at these keys: kernel_tag, seq_len_bin (0-32,33-64,65-128,129-256,256+), warmup_flag, batch_size_bin (1,2-4,5-8,9+).
3) For each bucket produced: p50, p90, p95, p99 of per-token latency and per-request tail (95/99).
4) Correlated with GPU counters sampled at 1 minute resolution and with sidecar scheduler logs to label stall reasons.

High-level findings (summary):
- Two dominant modes for per-token latency in seq_len 33-64: a low-latency flash kernel (~3.4ms/pkt p50) and a higher-latency fused-op fallthrough (~9.1ms/pkt p95).
- Kernel-handoff events concentrated at batch boundaries when batcher merges small outstanding requests; these show a 3x spike in kernel_start-to-exec latency for first token after handoff.
- Paged-attention path becomes competitive at seq_len >= 129 on GPUs with <48GB memory, but exhibits increased variance due to prefetch jitter.
- Warmup_flag true correlates with higher L2 misses and a longer p99 (~1.6x) indicative of priming the prefetch/paged pipeline.

Representative telemetry histogram (ascii):
- kernel_tag=flash | seq_len_bin=33-64 | batch_size_bin=1
  buckets: [0-1ms): 2%, [1-3ms): 46%, [3-6ms): 40%, [6-12ms): 10%, [12ms+): 2%
- kernel_tag=fused-op | same bins
  buckets: [0-1ms): 0.5%, [1-3ms): 6%, [3-6ms): 28%, [6-12ms): 44%, [12ms+): 21.5%
(Implication: mixture; fused-op path moves mass to higher-latency bins)

Sanity checks we ran:
- Replayed sampled traces to local microbench harness with identical kernel selection to validate telemetry labeling. That reproduced histogram modes within 5-8% error.
- Turned off coalescing in batcher to confirm that kernel-handoff spike disappears.

Experiment matrix (ideas and small actions):
- E1: Controlled microbench comparing flash vs paged vs fused-op for seq lengths 1, 16, 48, 128, 256; run on two GPU types (A100-40GB, A10x-24GB). Status: ran on A100, results in telemetry table attached to PR 1248.
- E2: Increase kernel-tag sampling to 10% for 3 routes for 48 hours to surface rare handoffs. Status: scheduled (weekend low-traffic window).
- E3: Synthesize warmup sequences that exercise prefix-cache to measure priming penalty and eviction behavior. Status: prototype harness committed.

Root-cause hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel switch cost: runtime path that chooses fused-op falls back to non-optimized kernels periodically when batch_size changes mid-request. Evidence: histogram spike aligned with batcher merge timestamps.
2) Prefetch jitter: paged-attn prefetch scheduling has contention with other kernels causing variance. Evidence: L2_util oscillations in GPU counters.
3) Alignment/stride mismatch: certain model layouts cause inefficient tensorcore tiling falling back to slower codepaths. Evidence: higher tensorcore_util but lower SM efficiency when fused-op selected.

Quick reproduction commands (microbench harness examples):
- python tools/attn_microbench.py --model redwood-3b-v1 --kernel flash --seq 48 --batch 1 --iter 5000 --device a100
- python tools/attn_microbench.py --model redwood-3b-v1 --kernel fused --seq 48 --batch 1 --iter 5000 --device a100
Notes: harness toggles environment variable RW_FORCE_KERNEL and emits per-token logs to local file for histogram reconstruction.

Observed anomalies (detailed):
- Anomaly A: intermittent 20-40ms first-token latency when batch_size merges from 1 to 2 (seen mostly on region-eu-2). Trace snippets show extra 1-2ms host scheduling plus a ~15-35ms wait inside kernel dispatcher trying alternate codepath.
- Anomaly B: paged-attn p99 spikes (500ms->900ms) correlated with a GC cycle on host side when kernel queue backs up.

Mitigations tried so far:
- Short-term: added jitter guard in batcher to avoid immediate merge of tiny requests (reduced A by ~70% in synthetic workload).
- Medium-term: instrumented kernel selector to emit pre-decision reasons (e.g., memory_budget_low, stride_mismatch). This helped classify 87% of fused-op fallthroughs.

Open action items and owners (two-week sprint):
- [Asha] Finish E2 sampling run and dump full histograms to GCS (deadline: 2026-02-20).
- [Marcus] Add transition traces to dispatcher to capture time between decision and kernel enqueue (deadline: 2026-02-17).
- [Diego] Run microbench matrix on A10x and post results to PR notes (deadline: 2026-02-22).
- [Priya] Draft a short runbook for operators when paged-attn p99 > 1s (deadline: 2026-02-18).

Notes to self (informal):
- When reproducing, keep network offload stable — seen cases where NVLink resets make numbers noisier.
- Remember to correlate workloads by route metadata (prod vs dev) — dev often has more token-level variance due to long prompt injection patterns.

Decisions to propose at retro:
- Adopt histogram-first telemetry dashboard for attention kernels (p50/p90/p95/p99 + modal decomposition).
- Make kernel_tag mandatory in trace payload for all hosted routes for 30 days after rollout of any kernel change.

Risks and unknowns:
- Increased sampling (10%) will incur ingestion and storage cost; need to budget and get sign-off from infra.
- Some fused-op fallthroughs appear hardware-specific (older SM arch) — risk of large divergence across customer fleets.

Appendix: quick checklist for a reproducible kernel-handoff case
- capture trace_id with full host and GPU counters
- run local microbench with same env and RW_FORCE_KERNEL unset and set to fused/flash
- compare histograms (p50/p90/p95/p99) and overlay with sampled trace token-times
- record PRs/changes if selector heuristics were tuned during case

Unresolved questions:
- Are there kernel hop patterns that repeat at specific times of day because of co-scheduled maintenance jobs? (need longer sampling)
- Can we expose a low-overhead kernel decision trace that doesn't blow up telemetry budget?

End of sprint notes.

-- Asha
